instructions: Pat the chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Sprinkle 1 tsp of the salt, the 1/2 tsp pepper and the 1 tsp herbes de Provence over both sides.

Set a large, deep skillet that has a lid over medium high heat with the 1 tbsp olive oil. When the oil shimmers, lay the thighs in skin side down, leaving a little room between them. Stand back a little. They'll spatter.

Leave them alone until the skin is deep golden and lets go of the pan on its own, 6 to 8 minutes. Meanwhile, dice the onion, mince the 2 garlic cloves, halve the cherry tomatoes and halve 1/2 cup of the olives.
Flip the thighs and cook the other side for 3 minutes, then transfer them to a plate, skin side up.
Pour off all but about 1 tbsp of the fat. Turn the heat to medium, add the onion and the last 1/4 tsp of salt, and cook, stirring now and then, until it's soft and see through, about 5 minutes.
Add the garlic and stir for 30 seconds, until you can smell it.
Pour in 1/2 cup of the wine and scrape up the browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Let it bubble for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and cook, stirring now and then, until they start to soften and split, 3 to 4 minutes.

Set the thighs back in the pan skin side up, along with any juices from the plate, keeping the skin above the sauce. Cover, turn the heat to medium low and cook for 25 minutes. You're cooking them to 175°F, so if you have a thermometer, check the thickest thigh near the bone. No thermometer? Cut into one next to the bone: it's done when the juices run clear and there's no pink.
Transfer the chicken to a plate. Take the pan off the heat and stir in the olives and 1 tbsp of the capers. Tear about 1/3 cup of the basil leaves into the sauce.
Taste the sauce. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Set the chicken back in the pan and spoon the sauce around it. Serve with the baguette, sliced.
method_notes: All three brown seasoned chicken, deglaze with white wine and cook it with tomatoes and olives. Mon Petit Four browns bone in thighs, softens onion and garlic, simmers the chicken covered with tomatoes and wine on the stove, then stirs in olives, capers and basil at the end. Averie Cooks and Vikalinka finish theirs in a 400°F oven, Averie Cooks with shallots, kalamatas and herbes de Provence, and Vikalinka with boneless breasts marinated in wine and herbs and a stock sauce thickened with flour. This one follows the lead's stovetop method and adds the 1 tsp of herbes de Provence from Averie Cooks to the chicken's seasoning.
